Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
ABRASIVE SPECIALITIES (BONDED) 

( First Revision ) 



1, Scope — Covers the dimensions and requirements for the following abrasive specialities; 

a) Rectangular sharpening stones (plain and combination); 

b) Sticks (square, triangular, round and half-round); 

c) Scythe stones; 

d) Slip stones; 

e) Rubbing bricks; and 

f) Reaper files. 

2. Types 

2.0 The following types shall be considered as standard, the basis of classification being the grit 
of the abrasive materials used. 

2.1 Rectangular Sfiarpening Stones, S//cAs, Scytfie Stones, Slip Stones and Reaper File 

Type Grit 

Coarse 80-120 

Medium 150-180 

Fine 220-320 

Extra fme ^ 400 and finer 

Note— Combination stones are usually available only in a combination of coarse and fine. 

2.2 Rubbing Briclis 

Type Grit 

Extra coarse 20-30 

Coarse 36-46 

Medium 60-80 

Fine 120-320 

Extra fine 400 and finer 

3. Abrasive and Bond 

3.1 The abrasive material used shall be either silicon carbide or aluminium oxide, as specified by 
the purchaser. 

3.2 Thebond used shall be of the vitrified type, but subject to agreement between the purchaser 
and the supplier, resin, silicate or shellac bond may also be used. 

4. Shapes and Dimensions 

4.1 The shapes and dimensions of the abrasive specialities shall be as given in Tables 1 to 
9 except for reaper file. 



Adopted 30 October 1979

4.2.1 The timber used for handle of reaper file shall conform to any of the timbers as specified

5. Performance Test — The bonded stone shall withstand a practical trial in consistence with its 
normal use. 



6 



18:1262-1979 

6. Marking— The abrasive specialities shall be legibly marked with the following: 

a) Designating size; 

b) Abrasive; 

c) Type (for example, coarse, medium or fine); and 

d) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — Each abrasive speciality shall be wrapped in paper to avoid soiling of its face by 
direct contact with the packing medium. Where cardboard or similar type of cartons are used, 
wrapping in paper may be dispensed with. A suitable number of items of the same type and size 
shall be packed face to face in a case. A suitable layer of cushioning material shall be kept 
between items and case, so as to avoid damage during handling. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1958. This revision has been necessitated mainly to 
delete the equivalent inch dimensions specified in it. Moreover, it has been observed that the 
industry has completely switched over to metric dimensions as far as abrasive specialities are 
concerned. 



Printed at Arcee Press, New Delhi 110055
